Well known is the butterfly effect, a system where it's not possible to predict how arbitrarily small changes in its initial conditions will affect the outcome.

This piece tries to achieve this with a few simple steps by manipulating uv-coordinates: rotate, distort, repeat n-times. Fitting the notion, the resulting images resemble butterflies. 

Btw, this is my genesis nft project.

To save a hi-res PNG (4096x4096 px), double click or hit 's' (give it a few seconds to generate).

fx(toadz) are Cryptoadz (cryptoadz.io) on fx(hash). Using the power of CC0 artwork, you can now acquire a toad on the Tezos blockchain.

Each toad is randomly generated at mint, trait rarities are based on the tx hash from mint and do not match "real" toadz rarities. The final distribution of attributes cannot be known until all fx(toadz) are minted.

None of the original 1/1, legendary, licked, or tall toadz are included in this collection - it is 100% randomly generated from the normal (short) toadz assets. Some traits have been removed to simplify rendering code: Matrix background, large fly lick mouth, top hats, mysterious hoodie, and a few more.

Artwork (PNG layers) is courtesy of the Cryptoadz team and toadztoolz.com (via CC0/public domain), randomization is powered by p5js and the fx(hash) platform.

Press 's' in live view to save a toad as a PNG.

5787.d:
Simple exploration of figure/ground generated from the flow of circles across an infinite field. Each composition is made up of a number of circles with a distance-based connective tissue of lines. Inspired by Nolli’s 1748 figure/ground drawing of Rome, the fields of color resemble expansive plazas, winding alleys, and building masses. Or do they resemble icebergs flowing across the sea? These generative bergburgs are both mountain and city. In a constant ebb and flow, the figures never repeat.

There are 4 primary colors used for foreground or background. There is a 1 in 13 chance of a unique color outside of the 4 primary colors to be used as foreground over a white background.

Press and hold mouse to reveal the generative circles. Press any key to reveal the network of lines.

5799.d:
Initially, I wrote some code to create rotating polygons to test my pen plotter. Then I realized that the motion of the polygons was interesting, so I connected the polygon vertices to try to visualize this motion.  The result was some interesting curves that varied with the number of polygons and vertices. 

The most interesting thing to me was the large number of different outputs that could be made from this simple process. There were many times during development when I got an output that was substantially different from what I had seen prior, even after thousands of iterations.  

Press s to save as an SVG.

Also, I highly recommend using a pen plotter to print out your primordial spiral.

	"Planet Color": black, monochrome, multicoloured
	"Planet Quantity": 3,4,5 or 8 planets
	"Planet Max Mobility": static, slow, high
	"Asteroid Quantity": 10, 15, 20 or 25 asteroids
	"Asteroid Sort Mode": None, X, Y, XY, Reversed XY
	"Density": 80, 10, 120 or 150 image creation steps

Lucy is an independent, generative automaton developed in MAX to compose songs in their entirety, using preset math parameters and virtual instrument patches that allow the insertion of variants to take the piece out of purely random scope.

In its MK4 version, the Maxlive code was readapted to generate 4 independent tracks, each for two measures, and then recorded variations of the same instrument until the performance fits with the others.

When collecting this work, the transaction hash will be used to determine the musical variations and visual features, having the following possible combinations:

3 Variations for percussion
3 Variations for the PAD
3 Variations for the FX Track
2 Variations for the lead synth
3 Variations for the pallet color
2 Variantions for the circle format

With 54 different combinations between the tracks, the Fourier transform is read to use the music as a reactive parameter to the generated visual forms. Wait for the IPFS content and click on canvas to play the song.

5914.d:
You are the product of countless tiny decisions taken over the course of your life. Stitched is an attempt to visualize one’s current self as a product of the myriad forking paths available to us. It is best appreciated in animated format: the latent structure unfolds in time; the past gradually fades away, tinted and obscure. 

Past decisions and missed opportunities leave a trail on the present. Psychology affects what you explore: drive controls how frequent one changes direction; indecisive mints explore many loose ends; balanced mints match complementary colours.

Stitched is adaptive to arbitrary screen resolution and aspect ratio, and best appreciated at high resolution. It initially renders with a large step size in time; pause and unpause to watch it unfold more gradually.

controls:

mouse click or space bar: pause / unpause / reset animation
s: save current frame

Inspired by The Garden of Forking Paths by Borges and stylistically by French and Russian Impressionists, and Autoglyphs by Larva Labs.

5994.d: In 1953, Robert Rauschenberg erased a drawing by Willem de Kooning. The act of erasure produced a new work that provoked thought on the immutability of art. "Erased Meridian" is an homage to Rauschenberg's performance. (Live mode displays a cropped detail.)
